A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RetimeGS work and contain 15 pages, including the four-page supplementary material with Appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, failure cases, and resource measurements in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C, including Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their numerical and qualitative results, including the supplementary analyses and resource measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same temporal-opacity formulation, Catmull–Rom trajectories, bidirectional flow supervision, triple rendering, dynamic stretching, relocation, and flow-aware initialization.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 10 DNA-Rendering scenes, nine Stage-Capture scenes, and Neural3DV Flame Steak and Flame Salmon sequences. The low-frame-rate failure scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. Tables 1, 3, 4, and 5 correct STGS citations from [44] to [18] and 2D Lifting citations from [28, 44] to [18, 28]; Section 4.2 already identifies these methods using [18] and FILM [28] in v1, establishing an attribution correction rather than a baseline replacement.

E3.justification: The camera usage, temporal holdouts, frame rates, 1K preprocessing, foreground PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS evaluation, training budgets, and supplementary comparison protocols remain identical.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablations in Table 2, low-frame-rate failures in Appendix B, dynamic-stretching analysis, optical-flow comparison in Table 6, and supplementary case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and the qualitative results remain unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains RetimeGS scores of 30.08 PSNR, 0.904 SSIM, and 0.0225 LPIPS; the corrected baseline citations do not alter scores or rankings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(8) are identical. No assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about temporal aliasing, continuous-time reconstruction, the proposed representation and training strategies, and performance under challenging motion.

C2.justification: The explanations of ghosting, flow supervision, and dynamic stretching are unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning unreliable flow under extreme motion or low frame rates and slight flickering between primitive groups.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information are unchanged, including PyTorch, the RTX 4090D GPU, Appendix A hyperparameters and 20,000 training iterations, Appendix C.10 resource measurements, and the project-page link.

R1.justification: Tables 1, 3, 4, and 5 correct source attribution for STGS and the reconstruction component of 2D Lifting from Yang et al. [44] to Li et al.'s Spacetime Gaussian Feature Splatting [18]. These are different works already present in both bibliographies; the broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited editorial changes update the arXiv version/date, correct table citations, and shorten reference [44]'s citation-page list. The prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10, table structures, captions, highlighting, and page layout are unchanged. The table edits are confined to citation markers beside existing method names.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes misleading baseline attributions in Tables 1, 3, 4, and 5, aligning them with Section 4.2 and the bibliography. This modestly improves accuracy and traceability. The scientific methods, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
